howto.name: Upload the PDF
howto.text: Select a PDF that contains one or more tables you need to extract as structured data.

howto.name: Select pages
howto.text: Choose specific pages or let the tool auto-detect all tables across the entire document.

howto.name: Pick the output format
howto.text: Choose CSV, Excel (.xlsx), or JSON. Each detected table becomes a separate sheet or file.

howto.name: Download the extracted data
howto.text: Click Extract. Tables are parsed using Camelot/Tabula and delivered in the chosen format inside a ZIP.

faq.a: CSV, Excel (.xlsx), and JSON. Each table is extracted separately and all results are packaged in a ZIP file.

faq.q: Can it extract tables from scanned PDFs?
faq.a: For best results, run OCR first using the OCR tool to create a text layer, then use table extraction. The tool works best with text-based PDFs.

faq.q: How does the tool detect table boundaries?
faq.a: It uses Camelot and Tabula libraries, which detect ruled lines and text alignment patterns to identify table structures. Tables without visible borders may need manual page selection.
